How we work

Independent thinking, delivered with rigour.

We are deliberately small and deliberately senior. That means fewer hand-offs, faster answers, and advice that is accountable to a name — not a department.

— 01

Question first

Every engagement begins by sharpening the question. A well-framed question is worth more than a hundred pages of unfocused analysis.

— 02

Evidence, then judgement

We separate what the data shows from what we think it means — and we show our workings, so your team can challenge every step.

— 03

Decisions, not documents

Our work ends when a decision is made and owned. Reports are a means to that end, never the end itself.

About us

A small practice with a single obsession: better decisions.

Blackwood Advisory was founded on a simple observation — organisations rarely lack information. They lack clarity about which information matters, and the confidence to act on it.

Our story

Built for the conversations that happen behind closed doors.

The practice brings together research, advisory, facilitation and speaking work that is usually scattered across four different suppliers — a research agency here, a consultancy there, an outside facilitator for the away-day, a speaker for the conference. Each hand-off loses context. Each supplier optimises for their own deliverable, not for your decision.

Blackwood Advisory exists to close those gaps. The same senior team that researches your market sits in the room when strategy is debated, facilitates the session where the decision is taken, and can carry the reasoning to your wider leadership audience. One line of accountability, from first question to final commitment.

We stay deliberately boutique. A short client list, senior people on every engagement, and the freedom to say “the evidence doesn't support that” — even when it isn't the comfortable answer.

Placeholder “Blackwood Advisory” is a placeholder brand for this design concept. The client's real name, story and visual identity will replace this content before launch.

Vision & values

What we believe

Our vision is a business culture where major decisions are made on evidence, argued honestly, and owned collectively. Four values govern how we work towards it.

Evidence over opinion

Rank and volume don't win arguments here. The strongest claim is the one that survives scrutiny of its sources.

Independence

We sell judgement, not implementation contracts or software. Our only incentive is to tell you what we actually think.

Discretion

Boardroom work stays in the boardroom. Client names, data and deliberations are never used for our marketing.

Candour with respect

We will challenge a room of executives — and do it in a way that leaves every relationship in that room stronger.

Our approach

How an engagement unfolds

01

Listen

A confidential conversation about the decision you face, the politics around it, and what “good” would look like. No pitch, no obligation.

02

Frame

We agree the precise question, the evidence needed to answer it, and how the answer will be used. This framing document anchors everything that follows.

03

Investigate

Research and analysis carried out by senior practitioners — interviews, data work and market study, with interim findings you can challenge as we go.

04

Decide & embed

Findings are worked through with your leadership team in a facilitated session, ending in a decision with named owners — and support while it beds in.

Research designed around your question — not sold off the shelf.

Syndicated reports describe the average business in your sector. You are not the average business. We design every study from a blank page: your market, your competitors, your decision.

Capabilities

What a bespoke study can answer

— 01

Market intelligence

Market sizing that goes beyond headline numbers: segment-level demand, growth drivers, and where value is actually concentrating.

— 02

Competitor analysis

Structured profiles of the competitors that matter — their positioning, pricing logic, strengths, and the gaps they leave open.

— 03

Customer & stakeholder insight

In-depth interviews and surveys that reveal why customers choose, stay or leave — in their words, not your assumptions.

— 04

Opportunity assessment

New markets, new segments, new offers. We test the opportunity against evidence before you commit serious capital to it.

— 05

Trend & foresight work

Scanning the regulatory, technological and social shifts approaching your sector — and what each scenario would demand of you.

— 06

Due-diligence support

Independent market and commercial evidence for acquisitions, investments and partnerships, delivered to transaction timescales.

Methods

Analytical capability, applied proportionately

We choose methods to fit the question and the deadline — never the other way round. A typical study blends several of the following, and every finding is traceable to its source.

  • Executive & expert interviewsConfidential depth interviews with industry participants, conducted by senior researchers.
  • Surveys & quantitative analysisDesigned, fielded and analysed in-house, with sample design you can defend.
  • Desk & data researchCompany filings, trade data, regulatory sources and published research, critically appraised.
  • Scenario & sensitivity workKey assumptions stress-tested, so you see the range of outcomes — not a single fragile forecast.

Advisory services

Senior counsel for strategy, change and the decisions in between.

Select a service below to see how an engagement works — what it covers, how it runs, and what your organisation takes away.

Why independent advice

No products to sell. No teams to keep busy.

Large consultancies earn more when projects grow. We earn our fee when your decision improves. That difference in incentives shapes everything: shorter engagements, franker advice, and recommendations we would defend even if they end the work sooner.

  • Principal-led, alwaysThe adviser you meet is the adviser who does the work.
  • Fixed, agreed scopeFees and deliverables settled in writing before work begins.
  • Challenge includedStructured dissent is part of the service — not an optional extra.

Not sure which service fits?

Most engagements start as a conversation, not a category. Book a consultation and we'll map the right approach together.

Facilitation

The right people in the room. The real issues on the table. A decision before you leave.

Poorly run leadership sessions are expensive theatre. Ours are designed backwards from the decision you need — then run with enough structure to be productive and enough candour to be honest.

Session formats

Designed around your room, your people, your decision

a.Strategic planning sessions

Annual and multi-year planning that starts from evidence, tests real options, and ends with priorities the whole team can repeat from memory.

b.Board & leadership away-days

Space away from the operational noise, structured so the difficult topics get airtime — not just the comfortable agenda items.

c.Stakeholder engagement

Sessions that bring partners, funders, regulators or community voices into the conversation constructively — with clear rules and honest reporting back.

d.Problem-solving workshops

Focused working sessions on a single knotty issue: a stalled project, a failing process, a partnership under strain.

How a session runs

Before, during and after the room

01

Design & pre-work

We interview key participants in advance, surface the real fault lines privately, and design the agenda around them. Participants receive a short evidence pack — not a slide deck to ignore.

02

The session itself

Tight facilitation: timed working blocks, structured challenge, and disagreement captured visibly rather than smoothed over. Decisions are recorded as they're made, in the room's own words.

03

Actions & follow-through

Within days, a concise record: decisions taken, owners named, dates agreed — plus a follow-up session to check the commitments actually moved.

Plan a session →
What changes

Meetings people describe as “the one where it finally got decided.”

Clients typically come to us after a strategy day that produced flip-chart paper and little else. The difference is preparation and nerve: preparation that loads the room with the right evidence, and the nerve to keep the conversation on the question that matters.

  • Decisions with ownersEvery session closes with named commitments, not sentiments.
  • Dissent on recordMinority views are captured, so revisiting a decision later is rational — not political.
  • Energy preservedStructure that protects the group's time and attention across a full day.

Planning an away-day or a difficult session?

Tell us who's in the room and what has to be true by the end of it. We'll design the rest.

Public speaking

Keynotes that respect the audience's intelligence.

No motivational filler, no recycled slide decks. Evidence-led talks on markets, strategy and decision-making — tailored to your audience and the moment your organisation is in.

Speaker profile

The Principal Consultant

The practice's founder speaks on the same subjects the consultancy researches: how markets really move, why strategies fail in the follow-through, and how leadership teams can make fewer, better decisions. Talks draw on live research work, so the examples are current and the data is real.

Formats range from 30-minute executive briefings to full conference keynotes and panel moderation, in person or virtual. Every engagement includes a pre-event call to align the talk with your audience's context.
